Advocate for the Respondent : Pp, Assam
 Before
Hon'Ble
Mrs. Justice Susmita Phukan Khaund

1. Heard Mr. B. Talukdar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner as well as Mr. B. Sarma,
learned Addl. P.P. appearing for the State respondent.

2. The petitioner, namely, Chandan Thakur, has filed this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C with prayer for pre-arrest bail as he is apprehending arrest in connection with Nagaon Sadar P.S. Case No. 213/2023, under Section 376/313/384 IPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions at the Bar with circumspection and I have perused the case diary.
4. The learned Addl. P.P. has raised serious objections stating that there are incriminating materials against the petitioner in the case diary.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent and a false case has been slammed against him.

It is submitted that the victim had a love affair with the petitioner and she has borrowed money from the petitioner and her mother issued a cheque of Rs.
30,000/- to the petitioner.
6.
There are indeed incriminating materials in the case diary.
7. At this juncture, there appears to be no justified ground to extent the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
8. Accordingly, this petition stands rejected at this stage of investigation.
Send back the case diary.
